@CHC-YHC could you do the second review for this PR? The relabelling was done by keyword on each rationale, so it needs a person to check it. Below is a random 10% sample (50 of the 505 MG.2.3 moves and 3 of the 25 GV.1.2 moves), with the official statement of each subcategory. For each row: does the rationale describe the new subcategory better than the old one? Y, N or ?, with a note for N and ?. If more than a few are N, I'll redo the classification before this goes anywhere.


- MG.2.3: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
- MG.2.4: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
- MG.1.3: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the map function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.
- GV.1.2: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.
- GV.2.1: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.

Update on the local check-rules-safety run: I stopped it after 2 h 55 min at full CPU, unfinished. It was re-running every one of the 538 rules touched by #779 and this PR against the benign corpora, and several of those rules are slow on long inputs (the ReDoS baseline lists some), so it never got through.

For this PR the gate cannot show anything new. Only `compliance.nist_ai_rmf` changed; the engine never reads `compliance`; and parsing all 511 files before and after shows every other field, detection included, is identical. So every rule matches exactly what it matches on main.

When this PR retargets to main, validate.yml will run the same gate in CI and may hit the same wall. A follow-up worth doing: have check-rules-safety skip rules whose detection, agent_source and test cases are unchanged from the base.
